Apple has updated its vintage and obsolete product lists today, with the iPhone X and 15-inch 2018 MacBook Pro now classified as obsolete. Here is an explanation of what this means.

iPhone X and 15-inch 2018 MacBook Pro now listed as obsolete

Apple today updated a support article titled "How to get service for your Apple products after they are no longer covered by a warranty," moving the 15-inch 2018 MacBook Pro and iPhone X from the vintage product list to the obsolete product list.

Apple explains that once a product is added to the obsolete list, the company stops providing all hardware repair services, and service providers are no longer able to order parts for it.

Products are typically not classified as obsolete until more than seven years after Apple has stopped selling them, but the actual timing of the classification is ultimately determined by Apple.

As for Apple's vintage product list, it includes products that Apple will only continue to repair on the condition that parts are still in stock. Apple defines a product as "vintage" when it has been discontinued for more than five years but less than seven years.

Apple began dropping major system support for the iPhone X starting with iOS 17, with iOS 16 being its last major system version. The device can now only be upgraded to iOS 16.7.16 at the highest. As for the 15-inch 2018 MacBook Pro, it can only support macOS Sequoia, and the latest version available for this model is macOS 15.7.7.

For a detailed look at Apple's complete vintage and obsolete product lists, as well as under what circumstances repair services can be extended for up to 10 years, you can click on this link to find out more.
